# Forecasting {.hero #s09-forecasting}

::: {.sem-mark data-sem="9"}
Seminar 9 · Exponential smoothing
:::

$\alpha$ is how much you trust the latest number.

::: {.lede}
$F_{t+1} = \alpha x_t + (1-\alpha)F_t$ looks like it only remembers one step back. Unfold it and every observation you have ever seen is in there — each one weighted a little less than the one after it.
:::

## The memory hidden in one line {.stage-slide #smooth-intuition}

::: {.stage-wrap .stage-wrap-std}
<div id="smooth-stage" class="stage"></div>
:::

[]{.fragment .fi-frag id="smooth-frag-1"}
[]{.fragment .fi-frag id="smooth-frag-2"}

::: {.slide-footer}
At $\alpha = 0.8$ the forecast is barely a forecast — it is last month's number with a delay. At $\alpha = 0.2$ it is so smooth it cannot turn a corner. Choosing $\alpha$ is choosing where on that line to stand.
:::

## Let the data pick $\alpha$ {.sim-slide #smooth-sim}

::: {.slide-kicker}
Seminar 9 · MSE and MAE
:::

::: {.lede-min}
This series **trends upward**, which breaks the no-trend assumption smoothing requires. $F_2 = 67$ is given; the error metrics will tell you the rest.
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-text}
```{webr-r}
x <- c(45, 62, 73, 87, 86, 95)   # <-- trending
err <- function(a) {
  f <- 67
  for (k in 2:5) f[k] <- a*x[k] + (1-a)*f[k-1]
  x[2:6] - f[1:5] }
for (a in c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8)) {
  e <- err(a)
  cat("a", a, " MSE", round(mean(e^2), 1),
      " MAE", round(mean(abs(e)), 2), "\n") }
```
:::

::: {.try-this}
Both metrics fall as $\alpha$ rises — the method is straining to keep up with a trend it was never built for. After the first month every error is *positive*: the forecast is late as soon as the trend takes hold. **Persistent one-signed errors are the diagnostic that you need a trend model, not a better $\alpha$.**
:::
